'''Cube''' is a format on [[GEMP]] (code <code>cube</code>) with a deck size of 40 cards. Its definition links to the Players Committee Cube page and is marked as not a game hall format.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="lib" />

== Deck size ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Default deck size on [[GEMP]]
| 40 cards
|}
The GEMP format definition sets a deck size of 40 cards.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="lib" />

== Players Committee Cube ==
The Players Committee calls it Watto's Chance Cube, or simply Cube. Players draft from "packs" made by shuffling a curated set of cards, instead of opening sealed product. Each Cube has fixed cards given to each player, hundreds of draftable cards, and add-on cards that come with some draftable cards.<ref name="pc-cube" />

The ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) describes two types of Watto's Cube event, "Traditional" and "Secret Squirrel". Both use 45-card decks.<ref name="afg" /> On play.swccg.com, GEMP sets the Cube format to 40 cards. The Players Committee GEMP code sets it to 45 cards.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp">[https://github.com/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/blob/5e26dd19cc700adbf77de53e0d7b89720c94f03e/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json swccgFormats.json], GEMP source code (PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public, commit 5e26dd19), GitHub. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021130403/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/5e26dd19/swccgFormats.json.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== GEMP cube and draft formats ==
* [[Watto's Cube with objective packs Cube]] (<code>wattos_cube_with_objective</code>)
* [[Watto's Cube with fixed pack Cube]] (<code>wattos_cube_with_fixed</code>)
* [[Premiere - Death Star II Draft]] (<code>basic_premds2_draft</code>)
* [[Premiere - Virtual Set 13 Draft]] (<code>basic_premv13_draft</code>)
* [[Premiere - Virtual Set 25 Draft]] (<code>holocron_premv25_draft</code>)
* [[Cube v7 + Objectives Draft]] (<code>c7obj_draft</code>)
All six have a deck size of 40 and link to the PC Cube page.<ref name="gemp" />
